Symbolic sums and products

Source: R/concrete-products.R, R/concrete-summations.R, R/concrete.R
summation.Rd

summation(f, list(i, a, b)) computes sum(f, i = a..b) in closed form with SymPy's Sum.doit(): direct sums of short ranges, telescoping, Faulhaber polynomials, geometric sums (a Piecewise for ratio 1), Gosper's algorithm, hypergeometric series through hyperexpand() (a Piecewise with the convergence condition), sums of rational functions over infinite ranges by residues, zeta sums and Kronecker deltas (deltasummation()). gosper_sum(f, k) is the indefinite Gosper sum. product(f, list(i, a, b)) is SymPy's Product.doit(): direct products of short ranges, rising factorials over the roots of polynomial factors, sums in exponents, and Kronecker deltas (deltaproduct()). Sum() and Product() build unevaluated objects; use doit(). is_convergent() applies standard convergence tests.

Usage

deltaproduct(f, limit)

deltasummation(f, limit, no_piecewise = FALSE)

summation(f, ...)

Sum(f, ...)

product(f, ...)

Product(f, ...)

gosper_sum(f, ...)

Arguments

f

The summand or factor.

limit

A limit list(i, a, b).

no_piecewise

Do not wrap the result in a Piecewise.

...

Limits list(i, a, b).

Value

An expression.

Examples

i <- Symbol("i", integer = TRUE); n <- Symbol("n", integer = TRUE)
summation(i^2, list(i, 1, n))
#> n^3/3 + n^2/2 + n/6
summation(1 / i^2, list(i, 1, oo))
#> pi^2/6
product(i, list(i, 1, n))
#> factorial(n)
